title: How to Start Online Meetings on a High Note
summary: The creator explains three simple strategies to start online meetings successfully by building rapport, giving thoughtful responses, and smoothly transitioning back to work. These techniques help make a strong, positive impression whether talking to new clients or team members.
key_points: When talking to a stranger or client you want to impress, stalk them on LinkedIn beforehand to see how long they have been in the industry.

Start the conversation by mentioning their tenure, e.g., 'Hey, I was looking forward to talking to you because you've been working in this industry for 10 years, right?' This makes them feel special and starts the call with a compliment.
When someone you already know (like a boss, manager, or team member) asks 'How are you?', do not just say 'I'm fine, I'm good, I'm okay'.
Give a better, more playful answer in return, such as sharing a small relatable story about making coffee while your son spooked you behind the kitchen door, leaving you with half a cup of coffee.

After building rapport and getting the conversation started on a good note, transition back to work by saying: 'By the way, I'm sorry, this is such a fun conversation, but I end up talking too much. I don't want to take away from what we're here to discuss. We wanted to talk about X, Y, and Z, right?'
content:
If you like tactics like this, follow for more :) Here's how to start online meetings the right way, because over the last nine and a half years, I've hired almost 400 people for my own businesses. And some days, I would have 10 to 15 meetings, some with my clients, some with my team. But I needed to figure out a way to start a call on a high, because at the end of the day, if the call doesn't start off good, most likely it's not going to end well as well. There's only three simple things that you need to remember. First, let's say if you're talking to a stranger or a client that you want to impress, rather than going straight into work conversations, what I want you to do instead is build a little bit of rapport. Now, the way you do this is by actually doing a little stalking on LinkedIn, finding out how long have they been in the industry. Then the start of the conversation becomes very simple: 'Hey, I was looking forward to talking to you because you've been working in this industry for 10 years, right?' Now, A, that makes them feel special because you did a little bit of research on them, but B, most importantly, you started off on a compliment, and everyone loves compliments, which helps you start the conversation on a high. The second point is when you're talking to someone that you already know, maybe someone on the team, maybe your boss, maybe your manager. You want to start the conversation with a little bit of rapport as well. Now, the way to do this is when you ask them 'How are you doing?', they're going to ask you that question back. Don't say, 'I'm fine, I'm good, I'm okay.' I want you to give a better answer in return. So, someone in our group program was struggling with this because they were talking to very wealthy clients every single day. It was the same people again and again, but she wasn't able to actually get into a conversation with them. So I said, 'Let's prepare a better answer.' And her answer is so good that even I use this again and again. So when her clients asked her how she was doing, rather than saying 'I'm okay', she would say, 'I was making a cup of coffee before this meeting, but my son was hiding behind the kitchen door and he spooked me, which is why right now, I'm sitting with half a cup of coffee.' And it's such a simple, fun, playful answer that immediately the other person goes into, 'Oh, that's so cute.' And then she would get to ask, 'What about you? Do you have kids?' And that way she would get into a conversation very smoothly, which leads me to the last point. Once you've built a little bit of rapport and the conversation gets started on a good note, then you want to bring it back to work. Now, the best way I've found to bring the conversation back to work is by just saying, 'Oh, by the way, I'm sorry. This is such a fun conversation, but I end up talking too much. I don't want to take away from what we're here to discuss. We wanted to talk about X, Y, and Z, right?' And then you transition into work. You don't need to talk for ages, you just need to show a little bit of your human side before you go into work conversations.
